title: Held Up
logline: A long-distance bus breaks down on a rural road. Passengers step out into the heat with nowhere to be but exactly here, and the mood of the group shifts, more than once, before it moves again.
human_question: What does a group of strangers do with an hour nobody chose?

premise.story: An ordinary breakdown on a rural route: the driver and conductor under pressure to fix or replace the vehicle, passengers stepping out, phone calls home, complaints, small kindnesses between strangers, and the mood changing as the wait lengthens.
premise.place: A rural highway between provincial towns, wherever the bus happens to stop.
premise.experience: The viewer waits with the passengers in real time: heat, boredom, irritation, and the small, unplanned generosities that also show up in a stalled crowd.

concept_links.why: This is the group's question in its plainest, least dramatic form: life refusing what a whole group of people want, which is simply to arrive [C007-P:L49]. The displeasure is felt first by each waiting person alone, and only afterwards passed between them.

Restlessness, present in every state of this kind, is a mind that will not settle on what is in front of it [C022-P:L73; C022-M:L19]. A stranded crowd shows that same unsettling spread across many people and many different ways of passing the time.

what_camera_could_observe: The moment the bus stops and passengers realise something is wrong
The driver and conductor working the problem, under pressure and under watch
Passengers stepping out: phone calls, complaints, waiting in shade
Small kindnesses: shared water, shared shade, help with luggage or children
The bus moving again, or a replacement arriving, and how the mood changes
what_must_be_real: The breakdown must happen on its own; it cannot be arranged, delayed, or timed to suit the crew, and it may not happen at all when the crew is present. If it happens, all passengers filmed must consent.

possible_arc.opening: A bus at speed, ordinary and full, then slowing unexpectedly.
possible_arc.turn: Time stretches and the group's mood turns, more than once, as the wait continues.
possible_arc.ending_open: However the journey actually resumes, or does not, within the filming window, ends the film.

requirements: A rural long-distance bus route where the crew can travel and wait without arranging events
A genuine, unplanned breakdown occurring during the filming window
Consent from the driver, conductor and passengers involved

suggestions.name: A rural highway between provincial towns
suggestions.region: Uva Province, on the Passara–Monaragala road corridor
suggestions.why: A long hill-to-dry-zone route served by long-distance buses, offering real distance and time for a stop to matter to passengers.
suggestions.verify: This is a plausible route type, not a confirmed filming plan; a specific service and willing operator must be found.

risks: Mocking frustrated people or singling anyone out at their worst moment
The breakdown cannot be arranged and may simply never happen on schedule
Passenger safety and comfort in heat or heavy traffic during a real delay
drop_if: No genuine, unplanned breakdown occurs within the filming window
Passengers do not consent to being shown

connections.note: Both are bounded-time ensemble pieces where a delay tests a crowd's patience in public.
Two waiting rooms of different kinds, a road and an office counter, testing the same small patience.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
